# aethersdr

**Linux client for FlexRadio transceivers**

- **Version recorded:** 26.8.1
- **Categories:** `rig-control`, `sdr-receivers`
- **Upstream:** <https://github.com/aethersdr/AetherSDR>

## What it does

Connects to a FlexRadio SmartSDR transceiver over the network and provides the operating interface: panadapter and waterfall, slice receivers, filter and mode control, transmit, and the metering the radio reports.

## Why you would want it

FlexRadio's own client software is Windows-only, and the radios are network-native -- the transceiver is a server and the front panel is software. That makes a Linux client the difference between using one from Linux and keeping a Windows machine on the desk purely to talk to it.

## Before it will work

A FlexRadio transceiver reachable on the network. Discovery is by broadcast, so a router between you and the radio usually means it is not found.

## Install and launch

- **Installed by name only** — it is in no profile.
- **Install:** `hammunition install aethersdr --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Its package ships its own commands and application-menu entry; a unit that ships none gets a generated terminal entry (**D-050**). `hammunition status` lists what is installed.
- **The install needs the network to:** your distribution's package archive.

## Offline use

*Not yet documented for this application.* Read “Before it will work” above for what it needs; the install-time network line above is the only offline fact generated from the manifest. Internet, a local network and a radio link are three different things, and this page does not claim any of them works until it says so.

## How it installs

- apt: `aethersdr`
  - **Only Kali carries this**, at 26.8.1+ds-1. No candidate on Debian 13, Ubuntu 26.04, Parrot or Mint (measured 2026-08-28). It is in the Blend's SDR task, which again tracks unstable rather than stable.

## Known problems

Reproducing a commercial vendor's protocol means feature coverage lags the vendor client and can break when the radio's firmware is updated -- check before updating firmware rather than after. The maintainer does not own this hardware, so nothing here is maintainer-verified (D-027); it is carried because other operators have it. Absent from four of the six targets, as above.
